answer: Agents settle via the haven netting house, posting every cipher receipt publicly. Receipts are key-bound and amount-bound, settling one identity once; reuse across keys is rejected on recomputation. Each identity locks a bond equal to its gross flow, not net flow: 500 moved locks 500; an honest agent pays once. The auditor recomputes each gross and stamps it with a saffron seal; unsealed settlements slash. A wash-cycle ring fails: the same 500 cannot cover two keys, and bonds stay locked until close. The k-th fake still locks a fresh 500, so 1000 fakes lock 500,000, one honest agent 500.
